character_description: Bond's love interest and contact in the 1954 TV adaptation.
Iconic beach emergence in Jamaica; independent survivalist gathering shells, captures Bond's attention but relies on Bond to escape Dr. No's lair.
First woman to meet James Bond at the London baccarat table, initiating the famous 'Bond, James Bond' line.
Dual-agent secretary working for the colonial government while reporting to Dr. No; traps Bond at her mountain home.
Soviet cipher clerk manipulated by SPECTRE who assists Bond across Europe and fatally shoots Rosa Klebb during the hotel climax.
The girlfriend of the Turkish MI6 contact Ali Kerim Bey.
Leader of Pussy Galore's Flying Circus, skilled martial artist and pilot who betrays Goldfinger by alerting the CIA and switching nerve gas canisters.
Helps Bond catch Goldfinger cheating at gin rummy; murdered by Oddjob via full-body gold paint asphyxiation.
Jill Masterson's sister, who tries to kill Goldfinger and is killed by Oddjob.
The masseuse seen with Bond in the Goldfinger pre-title sequence.
Sister of assassinated NATO pilot who turns against Largo, assists Bond underwater, and kills Largo with a harpoon gun.
Fierce, unrepentant SPECTRE operative and motorcycle assassin who mocks Bond's charm before being killed in the Junkanoo dance hall crossfire.
An MI6 agent in the Bahamas, captured and killed to avoid giving up information.
A physiotherapist at the Shrublands health clinic.
One of the many agents drawn into the 1967 spoof's 'multiple Bonds' plot.
Scottish widow and secret agent in the 1967 spoof.
Bond's daughter in the 1967 spoof, who infiltrates the villain's organisation.
One of the McTarry-sisters group in the 1967 spoof.
Moneypenny in the 1967 spoof.
One of the McTarry sisters in the 1967 spoof.
One of the McTarry sisters in the 1967 spoof.
A cameo in the 1967 spoof.
A supporting role in the 1967 spoof.
A supporting role in the 1967 spoof.
One of the McTarry sisters in the 1967 spoof.
Tiger Tanaka's top field operative who repeatedly rescues Bond in her custom Toyota 2000GT before being poisoned in her sleep.
Ama diver posing as Bond's wife who swims miles through shark-infested waters to summon ninja reinforcements for the volcano assault.
SPECTRE's senior agent in Japan, killed by piranhas after failing to kill Bond.
A Japanese masseuse who attends Bond.
The Chinese agent in the pre-title sequence; she returned as Madam Wu in 2006.
Complex, emotionally wounded noblewoman and ice racer who rescues Bond in a blizzard, battles Blofeld's henchmen, marries Bond, and is murdered on their wedding day.
One of Blofeld's 'Angels of Death' at the Piz Gloria clinic.
One of Blofeld's 'Angels of Death'; her film debut.
Sharp, opportunistic Amsterdam diamond smuggler with constantly shifting hair colors who assists Bond in Las Vegas and the oil rig showdown.
A flirtatious casino socialite, killed after being mistaken for Tiffany Case.
Clairvoyant psychic advisor to Kananga whose mystical abilities are tied to her virginity; escapes with Bond after he tricks her with a stacked deck.
First African-American Bond woman with a romantic link; rookie CIA agent blackmailed by Kananga who panics and is killed by a scarecrow gun.
Bond's Italian companion in the pre-title sequence.

film_title: The Man with the Golden Gun
character_description: MI6 administrative operative in the Far East whose comedic incompetence leads to her capture and nearly detonates Scaramanga's solar reactor.

film_title: The Man with the Golden Gun
character_description: Abused mistress who secretly mails the golden bullet to MI6 to orchestrate Scaramanga's assassination; shot dead at the Macau boxing arena.

film_title: The Man with the Golden Gun
character_description: A belly dancer in the Beirut nightclub scene.
Elite Soviet KGB major on a joint mission with MI6; professional equal to Bond who vows to kill him after the mission for shooting her lover.
Stromberg's helicopter pilot, who hunts Bond and is killed by a missile from his submerged Lotus.
The secretary to KGB head General Gogol; a former Miss World.
A hotel receptionist; she returned in Never Say Never Again.
NASA scientist on undercover CIA assignment evaluating Drax Industries; pilots the Moonraker shuttle and manually targets the globes in Earth orbit.
Hugo Drax's pilot, who helps Bond and is killed by Drax's dogs.
Greek-British marine archaeologist on a personal vendetta against Kristatos for assassinating her parents; wields a crossbow with deadly precision.
Teenage Olympic-hopeful ice skater sponsored by the smuggler Kristatos; infatuated with Bond, she throws herself at him and is put on a train home rather than seduced.
A countess and companion of the smuggler Kristatos, who is killed by his henchman Locque.
SPECTRE's flamboyant assassin, who tries to kill Bond with a string of improvised devices before being killed herself.
Mistress of the SPECTRE agent Largo, who turns against him and helps Bond.
Wealthy businesswoman and leader of the Octopus cult on a private floating palace in Udaipur; leads her troupe of acrobatic warriors to storm Kamal Khan's fortress.
Kamal Khan's associate who seduces Bond and later fights alongside Octopussy's troupe.
A member of Octopussy's all-female troupe.
California Division of Oil & Gas geologist defending her family company against Zorin; provides crucial fault line maps but frequently screams for rescue.
Superhumanly strong chief of security who betrays Zorin after he floods the mine with her inside; sacrifices her life to wheel the bomb out of the fault line.
One of Max Zorin's female associates in the plot to destroy Silicon Valley.
A Soviet KGB agent whose path crosses Bond's during the Zorin investigation.
Czechoslovakian cellist tricked by lover Koskov into acting as a fake sniper; pilots a cargo jeep and rides with the Mujahideen to save Bond at the airfield.
The girlfriend of the Soviet General Pushkin.
Tough, short-haired CIA pilot with a sawed-off shotgun who saves Bond in a barroom brawl and flies a crop duster into tanker trucks during the climax.
Drug lord Sanchez's girlfriend, who becomes Bond's ally.
Sole survivor of the Severnaya satellite facility massacre; hacks Boris Grishenko's mainframe, reprogramming the satellite to burn up in atmosphere.
Sadistic ex-Soviet fighter pilot who derives ecstasy from crushing opponents with her thighs; killed when Bond shoots her helicopter harness.

occupation: Colonel in Chinese Ministry of State Security
character_description: High-ranking Chinese intelligence operative with martial arts mastery, advanced gadgets, and equal field tactical command alongside Bond on the stealth ship.

occupation: Wife of Media Baron Elliot Carver
character_description: Bond's former lover who helps him break into Carver's broadcast center and is subsequently murdered by Dr. Kaufman.
A Danish language teacher and former lover of Bond.
A minor role in the film.
First female primary villain in the franchise who orchestrates the assassination of her father and manipulates Renard into causing a nuclear meltdown in Istanbul.
American nuclear physicist assisting in Kazakh nuclear weapons deconstruction; disarms weapon cores in a controversial tank-top costume.
A minor role in the film.
A minor role in the film.
The MI6 doctor who clears Bond for duty.
Elite NSA operative tracking Colonel Moon in Cuba; engages in sword fights and helicopter stunts with equal operational agency to 007.
Olympic fencing gold medalist and traitorous MI6 agent who betrays Bond in Iceland before being stabbed by Jinx with a dagger through The Art of War.
Sharp, sharp-witted HM Treasury accountant who matches Bond intellectually, undergoes severe trauma in the stairwell fight, and sacrifices herself in Venice to protect him.
Unhappy wife seduced by Bond in Nassau who inadvertently gives up Dimitrios's travel plans; found strangled in a hammock.
Bolivian operative seeking revenge against General Medrano for the murder of her family; notably has zero romantic or sexual intimacy with Bond throughout the film.
MI6 agent assigned to bring Bond back to London; seduced by Bond and drowned in crude oil in an homage to Goldfinger.
Rookie MI6 field agent who accidentally shoots Bond in Istanbul, assists in Macau, and chooses a desk job as M's assistant Moneypenny.
Former child sex-trafficking survivor enslaved by Silva; attempts to help Bond but is executed with a shot glass on her head on the abandoned island.
A brief role as Bond's lover; she had auditioned for the role of Sévérine.
Daughter of Mr. White who understands firearms and assassin psychology; rejects Bond's violent world before he saves her from the MI6 demolition.
Widow of assassin Marco Sciarra targeted by SPECTRE hitmen; saved by Bond in Rome. Made history as the oldest actress cast in a Bond romantic role (aged 50).
First lead Bond woman to carry over across consecutive films; mother of Mathilde whose childhood trauma with Safin drives the emotional core and resolution.
First Black female 007 agent; skilled operative with equal tactical command who infiltrates Safin's nanobot island fortress alongside Bond.
Charming, seemingly nervous Cuban CIA contact claiming only three weeks of training who unleashes devastating martial arts and firepower at the SPECTRE party.
